claim_verdicts.evidence: "a HorizontalPodAutoscaler automatically updates a workload resource (such as a Deployment...)"; "These resources each have a subresource named `scale`, an interface that allows you to dynamically set the number of replicas"; Figure 1: "HorizontalPodAutoscaler controls the scale of a Deployment and its ReplicaSet". manage-resources-containers.md: "When you create a Pod, the Kubernetes scheduler selects a node for the Pod to run on."

"The scheduler ensures that, for each resource type, the sum of the resource requests of the scheduled containers is less than the capacity of the node. Note that although actual memory or CPU resource usage on nodes is very low, the scheduler still refuses to place a Pod on a node if the capacity check fails." reserve-compute-resources.md: "'Allocatable' on a Kubernetes node is defined as the amount of compute resources that are available for pods. The scheduler does not over-subscribe 'Allocatable'."

Pending: "The Pod has been accepted by the Kubernetes cluster, but one or more of the containers has not been set up and made ready to run. This includes time a Pod spends waiting to be scheduled...". "If the scheduler cannot find any node where a Pod can fit, the Pod remains unscheduled... An Event is produced each time the scheduler fails to find a place for the Pod" (example: FailedScheduling ... insufficient cpu). Round 2: lesson's section 3 definition now matches.

Round 2 (claim text changed). "When provisioning, Cluster Autoscaler will add Nodes to the group that best fits the requests of pending Pods." "The main goal of provisioning is to make all Pods schedulable. This goal is not always attainable because of various limitations, including reaching configured provisioning limits..." "Autoscalers will make sure that the provisioned Nodes have enough resources to satisfy the requests. However, they don't directly take into account the real resource usage".

Round 2. "Autoscalers provision the Nodes by creating and deleting cloud provider resources backing them. Most commonly, the resources backing the Nodes are Virtual Machines." nodes.md: kubelet with --register-node (the default) registers itself; a node is "eligible to run a Pod" only when healthy. The comparison needs no number: the new-node path is the existing-node path plus machine creation, boot and registration. No duration is stated.

Round 2 (lesson now says evicts). "Removing non-empty Nodes during consolidation is disruptive—the Pods running on them are terminated, and possibly have to be recreated (for example by a Deployment). However, all such recreated Pods should be able to schedule on existing Nodes". Diagram: "Node autoscaler --> drain Nodes --> Kubernetes". "Consolidation, like provisioning, only considers Pod resource requests and not real resource usage".

issues.text: New in round 2. "holds several at once" is stronger than Npgsql documents: Minimum Pool Size defaults to 0 and idle connections above it close after Connection Idle Lifetime (300 s); the pool holds up to Maximum Pool Size (default 100), not always several. Also claim 14 records an Npgsql fact under version_key postgresql.
issues.quote: open connections the process keeps and reuses, up to a maximum size, so one Pod holds several at once
issues.fix: Replace "so one Pod holds several at once" with "so one Pod can hold several at once". In .meta.json, move the Npgsql sentence of claim 14 into its own claim with version_key npgsql.
